acceptance_criteria: Given/When/Then statements, each independently testable
_schema.cycle_done: cycle number that shipped it, or null

_notes: Product has no UI. 'backend' scope = plugin (C2), validation tooling (C1), installers (C5) and key provisioning (C6), all living under backend/. 'frontend' is false for every item.
FR-11: the shipped plugin must be ONE TypeScript file with zero runtime npm dependencies. Dev-only tooling (test runner, type-checker) is allowed.
External systems (Azure DevOps, az CLI, Bifrost, Kilo) are never called for real in tests; they are faked/mocked.

items.title: Project skeleton & CI
items.description: Architect picks the stack (expected: TypeScript, zero runtime deps, built-in or dev-only test runner) and records it in ADR-0001, including the supported Kilo version range and the layout under backend/ (plugin single file, validation tooling, installers, provisioning). Senior BE creates a minimal plugin stub and one smoke test. CI releaser wires scripts/ci.sh and GitHub Actions to a green pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean checkout, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` is run, Then it exits 0 and the output shows the backend package's type-check and test steps were executed (not the 'no packages yet' path).

Given the repository, When docs/architecture/ADR-0001-tech-stack.md is read by an automated check, Then the file exists and contains sections for language/runtime, test runner, supported Kilo version range, and the zero-runtime-dependency single-file plugin constraint (FR-11).

Given the backend package, When the test suite runs, Then a smoke test imports the single plugin source file (e.g. backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts) and asserts it exports a plugin function that, when invoked with a minimal fake Kilo context, returns an object exposing a `config` hook.
Given backend/package.json, When an automated check inspects it, Then the `dependencies` field is absent or empty (only devDependencies are allowed).
Given a push or pull request to main, When the GitHub Actions CI workflow runs, Then it executes `bash scripts/ci.sh` (verifiable by a check that .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes scripts/ci.sh).
Given the plugin stub, When its `config` hook is invoked with a config object, Then it resolves without throwing and leaves the object unchanged (no-op until F-features land).

items.title: Plugin: JSONC parser
items.description: FR-4 / AC-5. Pure, exported function (e.g. `parseJsonc(text: string): unknown`) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Strips line/block comments and trailing commas outside strings, then JSON.parse. Zero runtime deps (FR-11). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006).
acceptance_criteria: Given JSONC with `//` line comments and `/* */` block comments (including a multi-line block comment and a comment at end of file without trailing newline), When parsed, Then the result deep-equals the same document without comments.
Given JSONC with trailing commas in objects and arrays (including nested and with whitespace/comments between the comma and the closing bracket), When parsed, Then it parses to the expected object.
Given string values containing `https://host/path`, `/* not a comment */` and a literal `,}` sequence, When parsed, Then each string value is preserved exactly.

Given strings containing escaped quotes (`\"`) and escaped backslashes (a string ending in an escaped backslash, e.g. JSON source `"C:\\"`) followed by `//`, When parsed, Then string boundaries are respected and content is preserved.

Given invalid JSONC (unterminated string, unterminated block comment, or malformed JSON), When parsed, Then an Error with a descriptive message is thrown and the input text is not echoed in full in the message.

Given the Appendix A example from VISION.md, When parsed, Then provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equals `https://bifrost.yourcompany.internal/v1` and provider.bifrost.models has keys `azure/gpt-5` and `azure/gpt-5-mini`.
Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and backend/package.json still has no runtime `dependencies`.

items.title: Plugin: {env:} and {file:} placeholder resolution
items.description: FR-5 / AC-8. Pure helper exposed as `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Recursively resolves `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` placeholders in the parsed shared config and returns `{ value, unresolved }` where `unresolved` is a list of placeholder names (never values). Environment, home directory and file reader are injectable for tests (defaults: process.env, os.homedir(), fs.readFileSync). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006). Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given `{"x": "{env:SET_VAR}"}` and an injected env with SET_VAR=abc, When `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` runs, Then result.value.x equals `abc` and result.unresolved is empty.

Given `{"x": "{env:MISSING}", "y": 1}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then key x is absent from result.value (not present as undefined/empty), y equals 1, and result.unresolved contains exactly `env:MISSING`.
Given `{"x": "pre-{env:MISSING}-post"}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then x equals `pre--post` and result.unresolved contains `env:MISSING`.

Given `{"x": "{file:~/secret.txt}"}` and secret.txt containing `  s3cret\n` under an injected fake home directory, When resolved, Then x equals `s3cret` (trimmed) and the file read targeted `<home>/secret.txt` (`~/` expanded).

Given `{file:...}` that cannot be read (missing path, a directory, or a reader that throws with the file contents in its error message), When resolved, Then the key is dropped, result.unresolved contains `file:<path as written>`, and no returned or thrown value contains the file contents or the reader's error text.

Given placeholders nested in objects and arrays (e.g. `{"a":{"b":["{env:SET_VAR}","{env:MISSING}","keep"]}}`), When resolved, Then nested values follow the same rules, an array element that is only an unresolved placeholder is removed from the array (giving `["abc","keep"]`), and non-string values (numbers, booleans, null) and strings without placeholders are returned unchanged.

Given any input object, When resolved, Then the input object is not mutated, own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` in the input do not pollute Object.prototype, and a string containing multiple placeholders (`{env:A}/{env:B}`) resolves each one.

Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `resolvePlaceholders` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: in-place merge with defaults/enforce modes
items.description: FR-6 / AC-6 / AC-7. Pure helper exposed as `__internals.mergeConfig(target, shared, mode)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Deep-merges the (already parsed and placeholder-resolved) shared config into Kilo's resolved config object, mutating `target` in place. Plain objects are merged recursively; arrays and scalars are leaf values whose conflict is decided by mode (`defaults`: local wins; `enforce`: shared wins); a key absent locally is added from shared in both modes. Top-level `$schema` and `plugin` in the shared config are ignored. Any `apiKey` key at any depth in the shared config is never applied (local apiKey always preserved; vision AC-6, FR-12). Values copied from shared are deep-cloned so target never aliases shared. An unrecognised mode is treated as `defaults` (conservative). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006). Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given local `{model:'a'}` and shared `{model:'b', small_model:'s'}`, When `__internals.mergeConfig` runs in `defaults` mode, Then target.model equals `a` and target.small_model equals `s` (shared-only keys are added).

Given local `{model:'a', provider:{bifrost:{options:{baseURL:'L'}}}}` and shared `{model:'b', provider:{bifrost:{options:{baseURL:'S'}}}}`, When merged in `enforce` mode, Then target.model equals `b` and target.provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equals `S`; and When merged in `defaults` mode, Then both local values are kept (AC-7).

Given local `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey = 'sk-bf-local'` and a shared provider.bifrost block whose options contain `apiKey: 'sk-bf-shared'` plus `baseURL`, When merged in `defaults` and in `enforce` mode, Then apiKey still equals `sk-bf-local`, baseURL is merged per mode, and with a local config that has no apiKey the shared apiKey is not added (AC-6).

Given local keys absent from the shared file at top level and nested (e.g. `provider.other`, `provider.bifrost.options.headers`, `agent.x`), When merged in either mode, Then those keys and their values are unchanged.
Given a shared config with top-level `$schema` and `plugin`, When merged in either mode, Then the local `$schema` and `plugin` values are unchanged, and when absent locally they are not added.

Given a target object, When merged, Then the function mutates and keeps the same target reference (including existing nested object references such as target.provider), the shared input is not mutated, and mutating a nested object or array in shared after the merge does not change target.

Given arrays or type conflicts (local `instructions:['a']` vs shared `['b','c']`; local object vs shared string), When merged, Then arrays are replaced wholesale (never concatenated) and conflicts resolve by mode (`defaults` keeps local, `enforce` takes shared), and an unrecognised mode behaves as `defaults`.

Given a shared config parsed from JSON containing own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` at top level and nested, When merged, Then Object.prototype is not polluted and no such key alters target's prototype; and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `mergeConfig` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: settings resolution (options, env, defaults)
items.description: FR-1 / FR-8 (and the settings half of FR-3). Pure helper exposed as `__internals.resolveSettings(options, deps?)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Resolves org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, pat, timeoutMs with precedence: plugin option (non-empty string / finite number) > KILO_AZDO_* env var (KILO_AZDO_ORG, KILO_AZDO_PROJECT, KILO_AZDO_REPO, KILO_AZDO_PATH, KILO_AZDO_BRANCH, KILO_AZDO_MODE, KILO_AZDO_PAT, KILO_AZDO_TIMEOUT_MS) > built-in default (path `/kilo.jsonc`, branch `main`, mode `defaults`, timeoutMs 5000; org/project/repo/pat have no default). Returns `{ settings, missing, warnings }` where `missing` lists required setting names (org, project, repo) that are unset and `warnings` are fixed messages naming settings only, never values. Env is injectable (default process.env, own properties only). The AZDO_PAT / AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT fallback and the az token belong to F-005; logging through Kilo's logger is wired in F-006. Not yet wired into the server/config hook. Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given options `{org:"opt"}` and an injected env with KILO_AZDO_ORG=env, When `__internals.resolveSettings` runs, Then settings.org equals `opt`; and Given no `branch` option and KILO_AZDO_BRANCH=dev, Then settings.branch equals `dev` (option > env precedence verified for each of org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, pat, timeoutMs).

Given no options (undefined) and an empty env, When settings resolve, Then path is `/kilo.jsonc`, branch is `main`, mode is `defaults`, timeoutMs is 5000, org/project/repo/pat are undefined, and `missing` deep-equals ["org","project","repo"].

Given mode `enforce` from options or from KILO_AZDO_MODE, When settings resolve, Then mode is `enforce`; and Given an invalid mode (e.g. `force`, `ENFORCE`, a number) from options or env, When settings resolve, Then mode is `defaults` and `warnings` contains an entry naming `mode`.

Given timeoutMs 3000 as an option number, or KILO_AZDO_TIMEOUT_MS=`2500` in env, When settings resolve, Then timeoutMs is 3000 or 2500 respectively; and Given a non-numeric, zero, negative, NaN, Infinity or non-integer value (option or env), When settings resolve, Then timeoutMs is 5000 and `warnings` contains an entry naming `timeoutMs`.

Given options that are null, an array, a string or a number, or option values of the wrong type (number for org, object for branch) or empty/whitespace-only strings, When settings resolve, Then no error is thrown and each such value is ignored so the env value or default applies; string values are trimmed, and a path without a leading `/` (e.g. `teams/a/kilo.jsonc`) is normalised to `/teams/a/kilo.jsonc`.

Given a `pat` option and KILO_AZDO_PAT both set, When settings resolve, Then settings.pat equals the option value; and Given any input containing a pat value (valid or wrongly typed), When `missing`, `warnings` and any thrown error are inspected, Then none of them contains the pat value.

Given inputs, When settings resolve, Then the options object and env are not mutated, an env created via Object.create({KILO_AZDO_ORG:"inh"}) does not supply org (own properties only), and own keys `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` in options do not pollute Object.prototype or the returned settings.

Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `resolveSettings` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: Azure DevOps fetch and authentication
items.description: FR-2 / FR-3 / FR-8. Async helper exposed as `__internals.fetchRemoteConfig(settings, deps?)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Takes the output `settings` of `resolveSettings` (F-004, contract 0.5.0; `settings.pat` already covers the plugin option and KILO_AZDO_PAT) and fetches the shared file via the Azure DevOps Git Items API. Returns a discriminated result `{ ok: true, text }` or `{ ok: false, error }` where `error` is a fixed, value-free code/message (e.g. invalid-settings, auth-unavailable, timeout, http-<status>, too-large, bad-response, network); it NEVER throws or rejects (FR-10). Injectable deps: `fetch` (default globalThis.fetch), `env` (default process.env, own properties only), `runAz` (default: node:child_process execFile without a shell, bounded by timeoutMs), and timer/AbortController seams as the Architect sees fit. Request uses `Accept: application/json`; the file text is read from the JSON body's `content` string. Lone UTF-16 surrogates in settings (security low finding 1, cycle 0006) must be handled here: either an `isWellFormed()` guard via a contract amendment or catching URIError during URL building. Parsing, placeholder resolution, merge, cache and logging stay in F-006. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11); Node built-ins only.
acceptance_criteria: Given settings {org:'my org', project:'plat form', repo:'kilo-config', path:'/teams/a b/kilo.jsonc', branch:'release/1', timeoutMs:5000} and a fake fetch, When `__internals.fetchRemoteConfig` runs, Then exactly one GET is sent to `https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/git/repositories/{repo}/items` with org/project/repo percent-encoded as path segments and query parameters path, versionDescriptor.version=<branch>, versionDescriptor.versionType=branch, includeContent=true and api-version=7.1 (all values percent-encoded), with an `Accept: application/json` header; and Given a 200 response whose JSON body has `content` equal to a JSONC string, Then the result is `{ ok: true, text }` with text equal to that string byte-for-byte (not parsed).

Given PAT sources, When the request is built, Then the Authorization header is `Basic ` + base64(':' + pat) using the first available of: settings.pat (plugin option or KILO_AZDO_PAT, from resolveSettings), then injected env AZDO_PAT, then AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (empty/whitespace-only values skipped, env read as own properties only); and in every PAT case the injected az runner is never invoked.

Given no PAT from any source, When fetching, Then the injected az runner is invoked once with arguments starting `account get-access-token --resource 499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798` (no shell), the trimmed returned token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; and Given the runner throws, exits non-zero, times out or returns empty output, Then no HTTP request is sent and the result is `{ ok: false }` with a fixed auth-unavailable error.

Given a fake fetch that never responds, When fetching with timeoutMs 50, Then the request's AbortSignal is aborted at the timeout and the result is `{ ok: false }` with a timeout error within a bounded time (no hang), and the default timeout when settings come from resolveSettings defaults is 5000 ms (FR-8).

Given a non-2xx response (e.g. 401, 404, 500), or a fetch that rejects with an error whose message contains the PAT, When fetching, Then the result is `{ ok: false }` and the error includes the HTTP status number for non-2xx responses, while no returned error contains the PAT, the bearer token, the Authorization header value or the underlying error's message.

Given a response larger than 1 MiB (declared by Content-Length or actual body length when the header is missing or lies), or a 200 body that is not JSON or lacks a string `content` field, When fetching, Then the result is `{ ok: false }` with a too-large or bad-response error and no oversized text is returned (cap enforced before any parsing; parseJsonc memory is about 50x input size).

Given settings with missing org/project/repo, or a value containing a lone surrogate (e.g. org `�`) that passed resolveSettings, When fetching, Then no URIError or other exception escapes, neither fetch nor the az runner is called, and the result is `{ ok: false }` with an invalid-settings error that names no values.

Given any input including hostile values (null/non-object settings or deps, throwing fetch, throwing env proxy), When `fetchRemoteConfig` runs, Then the returned promise always resolves (never rejects) and the settings/env objects are not mutated; and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `fetchRemoteConfig` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: cache, fallback, logging and never-crash wiring
items.description: FR-7 / FR-9 / FR-10 / AC-3 / AC-4 / AC-6 / AC-7 / AC-8 / AC-9, startup steps 2-6. Wire the shipped helpers (resolveSettings, fetchRemoteConfig, parseJsonc, resolvePlaceholders, mergeConfig) into the plugin's exported `config` hook inside the single file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Flow: resolve settings from plugin options + env; if `missing` is non-empty skip the fetch (log setting names only) and use the cache path; otherwise fetch; parse and validate the fetched text (root must be a plain object); on success write the cache, on any failure read the cache; resolve placeholders on the chosen config; merge in place with settings.mode. Cache: `<home>/.cache/kilo-azdo/remote-config.json`, holding the parsed shared config BEFORE placeholder resolution (PO decision: resolved {env:}/{file:} values may be secrets and must never be written to disk); directory created if missing; file mode 0600 on POSIX; written atomically (temp file + rename) so a crash never leaves a half-written cache; the cache content is validated on read exactly like fetched content. Logging goes through Kilo's logger with `service: azdo-remote-config` (Architect decides the exact Kilo logger API and keeps an injectable logger seam for tests); only fixed messages, setting names, error codes and placeholder names are logged, never values, and `settings` is never passed to the logger as an object. Trust boundary (cycle 0007 security info 4): the Architect records in an ADR which Kilo config layers may supply org/project/repo/path/pat and that fetched and cached content is treated as untrusted input (validated before merge; apiKey never applied, already enforced by mergeConfig). Deps (home dir, fs, fetch, env, runAz, logger) are injectable; tests never touch the real home directory or network. The Windows case-insensitive process.env note moved to T-012. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given complete settings in plugin options, a fake fetch returning a shared JSONC with comments and `{"model":"shared","small_model":"s","provider":{"bifrost":{"options":{"baseURL":"https://b/v1","apiKey":"sk-bf-shared"}}}}`, and a Kilo config `{model:'local', provider:{bifrost:{options:{apiKey:'sk-bf-local'}}}}`, When the plugin's `config` hook runs in `defaults` mode, Then the same config object is mutated in place with model `local`, small_model `s`, baseURL `https://b/v1` and apiKey `sk-bf-local`; and in `enforce` mode model becomes `shared` while apiKey stays `sk-bf-local` (AC-6, AC-7).

Given a successful fetch and a fake home directory without `.cache/kilo-azdo/`, When the hook runs, Then `<home>/.cache/kilo-azdo/remote-config.json` is created containing the parsed shared config with placeholders still unresolved (no resolved env/file value is written to disk), the write is atomic (temp file + rename), and on POSIX the file mode is 0600; and an info log with service `azdo-remote-config` states the remote source was used.

Given the fetch fails (e.g. timeout or http-500) and a valid cache file exists, When the hook runs, Then the cached config is placeholder-resolved and merged into the config, the cache is not overwritten, and a warn-level log with service `azdo-remote-config` names the fixed error code (AC-3).

Given the fetch fails and no cache exists, or the cache file is corrupt, not JSON, or has a non-object root, When the hook runs, Then the config deep-equals its original value, an error-level log is written with a fixed message, and a corrupt cache is never merged (AC-4).

Given resolved settings with `missing` non-empty, When the hook runs, Then neither fetch nor the az runner is called, the log names only the missing setting names (e.g. `org`), the cache fallback of the previous criteria applies, and each resolveSettings warning is logged at warn level; and Given fetched text that is invalid JSONC or whose root is not a plain object (array, string, number, null), When the hook runs, Then it is neither merged nor cached and the cache fallback applies.

Given a shared file containing `"x": "{env:MISSING}"` and `"y": "{env:SECRET_VAR}"` with SECRET_VAR set to `s3cr3t-value`, When the hook runs, Then config.x is not set, config.y is `s3cr3t-value`, and the logs name `env:MISSING` but contain neither `s3cr3t-value` nor any other placeholder value (AC-8).

Given a run with a PAT in plugin options, a bearer token returned by a fake az runner (PAT-less run), an `sk-bf-` apiKey in the local config and a resolved secret placeholder, across the success, cache-fallback and exception paths, When every argument of every logger call is captured and serialised (including util.inspect with showHidden), Then none contains any of those secret values, and the logger never receives the settings object (AC-9, FR-9).

Given each internal failure in turn (fetch dependency rejecting, parseJsonc throwing, unwritable cache directory, cache write throwing, logger throwing, a frozen Kilo config making mergeConfig throw TypeError, options null or non-object), When the hook runs, Then it resolves without throwing, any logged message is fixed text (never err.message), and Kilo's config is left either unchanged or fully merged (FR-10); and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and docs/architecture contains an ADR stating which config layers may supply org/project/repo/path/pat and that fetched/cached content is validated as untrusted before merge.

items.title: Shared config repo: example kilo.jsonc and validation script
items.description: FR-12 / FR-13 / AC-13. Template content for C1 plus a zero-dependency validator CLI used by the PR pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Given the shipped example /kilo.jsonc, When validated, Then the validator exits 0.
Given a file containing an `apiKey` field at any depth, When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero and names the JSON path.
Given a file containing a string matching `sk-bf-`, When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero without printing the full secret.
Given a file with invalid JSONC, When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero with a parse error.
Given a file whose structure violates the vendored Kilo config schema subset (e.g. `provider` not an object), When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero.
Given a shared config containing a relative {file:} path, bare ~, ~user or UNC-style path, When validated, Then the validator warns that it will never resolve.

Given a shared config whose baseURL host is outside an expected set, or containing keys named like Object.prototype members (hasOwnProperty, toString), When validated, Then the validator warns/fails accordingly (security findings from cycle 0005).

items.title: Shared config repo: Azure Pipelines PR gate and branch policy setup
items.description: FR-13 / FR-14. azure-pipelines.yml running the validator on PRs, and a script (az repos policy) that applies the main branch policy.
acceptance_criteria: Given azure-pipelines.yml, When parsed by a test, Then it triggers on PRs to main and runs the validator against kilo.jsonc and teams/*/kilo.jsonc.

Given the branch-policy script run in dry-run mode, When executed, Then it prints `az repos policy` commands for: minimum 1 reviewer, required platform-team reviewer group, and build validation on the pipeline.
Given the branch-policy script without required arguments, When executed, Then it exits non-zero with usage help.

items.title: Personal config template
items.description: FR-16 / FR-17. Template matching Appendix B. Cycle 0006 architect follow-up: the template must write `org`, `project` and `repo` explicitly (repo has no default since contract 0.5.0).
acceptance_criteria: Given the template, When parsed, Then its top-level keys are only `$schema`, `plugin` and `provider`.
Given the template, When inspected, Then `plugin` has exactly one entry pointing at `./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` with options org, project, repo, path, branch, mode.
Given the template, When inspected, Then `provider` contains only `bifrost.options.apiKey` with a placeholder value that does not match a real key pattern.
Given the template, When validated by the F-007 validator's secret check, Then no real `sk-bf-` secret is detected (placeholder only).

items.title: Bootstrap installer for macOS/Linux (install.sh)
items.description: FR-18..FR-23 / AC-12 / AC-14 for POSIX. Tests run with a temp HOME and faked az/curl. The installer must write org, project and repo explicitly into the plugin options (repo has no default since contract 0.5.0).
acceptance_criteria: Given a temp HOME with no Kilo config, When install.sh runs, Then the plugin is at `~/.config/kilo/azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` and the personal config is created from the template.
Given an existing personal config with other keys, When install.sh runs, Then only the plugin entry and apiKey are added/updated and other keys are preserved.
Given install.sh, When it runs, Then nothing is written to `~/.config/kilo/plugin/` (plugin loads exactly once, AC-12).
Given az missing and no PAT, When install.sh runs, Then it prints a clear fix and exits non-zero.
Given install.sh is run twice, When the config directory is diffed, Then the second run changed nothing except the plugin file (AC-14).
Given faked AzDO and Bifrost endpoints, When the smoke test step runs, Then it reports pass or fail for both checks without printing the key.

items.title: Bootstrap installer for Windows (install.ps1)
items.description: FR-18..FR-23 / AC-12 / AC-14 for Windows, behaviour parity with install.sh. Tests via Pester or pwsh where available; skipped with a clear message otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Given a temp USERPROFILE with no Kilo config, When install.ps1 runs, Then the plugin and personal config are created as with install.sh.
Given an existing personal config with other keys, When install.ps1 runs, Then other keys are preserved.
Given install.ps1, When it runs, Then nothing is written to the auto-loaded plugin directory.
Given az missing and no PAT, When install.ps1 runs, Then it prints a clear fix and exits non-zero.
Given install.ps1 is run twice, Then the second run changes nothing except the plugin file.

items.title: Key provisioning: create virtual key per engineer
items.description: FR-24 / FR-27. CLI calling Bifrost governance API (faked in tests).
acceptance_criteria: Given an email, budget, rate limit and model list, When `create` runs, Then one POST to the governance virtual-keys endpoint is made with name = email and those limits.

Given a successful create, When output and logs are captured, Then the key value is never printed to stdout/logs; it is written only to a per-engineer file with 0600 permissions (or delivered via a pluggable secure-channel hook).
Given a governance API error, When `create` runs, Then it exits non-zero with the HTTP status and no admin token in output.
Given the admin token, When the tool runs, Then it is read from an env var, never from a CLI argument or the shared repo.

items.title: Key provisioning: bulk CSV, list and disable (offboarding)
acceptance_criteria: Given a CSV of engineers where some already have keys, When `bulk` runs, Then keys are created only for engineers without one (no duplicates).
Given `bulk` is run twice with the same CSV, Then the second run creates nothing.
Given `list`, When run, Then it prints engineer names and key status without key values.
Given `disable alice@x`, When run, Then only alice's key is disabled and no other key is modified (AC-11).
Given `disable` for an unknown email, When run, Then it exits non-zero and modifies nothing.

items.title: End-to-end simulated startup test
items.description: AC-1 / AC-2 / AC-10 simulated: local fake AzDO + fake Bifrost servers exercise the whole plugin flow.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fake AzDO server serving a shared kilo.jsonc, When the plugin config hook runs, Then the resulting config lists the Bifrost models (AC-1, simulated).
Given the shared file changes on the fake server, When the hook runs again, Then the new value is in effect with no other change (AC-2).
Given the fake Bifrost enforces auth, When a request without a virtual key is made, Then it is rejected with 401 and the installer smoke test reports fail (AC-10, simulated).

items.title: Per-team config files support
items.description: FR-15. Example /teams/<team>/kilo.jsonc and validation coverage; plugin `path` option selects it.
acceptance_criteria: Given path `/teams/payments/kilo.jsonc`, When the plugin fetches, Then the request targets that path.
Given an example team file, When validated, Then the validator exits 0.
Given a team file with an apiKey, When the pipeline validator runs over teams/*, Then it fails.

items.title: User and operator documentation
items.description: Engineer setup guide, platform-team runbook (config change, key provisioning, offboarding), KILO_PURE caveat, supported Kilo version range, Phase 0 assumptions A1-A3 checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Given docs/, When an automated check runs, Then engineer setup, platform runbook and troubleshooting pages exist and link to each other.
Given the troubleshooting page, When checked, Then it mentions KILO_PURE=1, az login and the cache location.
Given all docs, When scanned for `sk-bf-` followed by real-looking key material, Then none is found.

items.title: Harden FR-11 lint against import evasions
items.description: Security/review: backend/tools/check-fr11.mjs regexes can be bypassed (template-literal or variable import(), createRequire, a "/*" string literal). Use ts.preProcessFile/AST, reject non-literal import() and createRequire, and add fixtures for these plus untested branches (export-from, bare import, missing/invalid package.json, missing plugin/, --root without value).
acceptance_criteria: Given a plugin file using import(`lodash`), import(variable), createRequire, or a "/*" string hiding an import, When check-fr11 runs, Then it exits 1.
Given fixtures for export-from, bare import, missing/invalid package.json, missing plugin/ and --root without a value, When tests run, Then each is covered and behaves as specified.

items.title: Release build step packaging the plugin file
items.description: Copy plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts to backend/dist/ so release.yml attaches it as an artefact; fits with the installer items.
acceptance_criteria: Given a release, When release.yml runs, Then backend/dist/azdo-remote-config.ts is attached and byte-identical to the source.

items.title: Escape raw BOM literal and lint invisible characters
items.description: PO cycle 0005: the BOM constant is already written as the ASCII escape (verified, line 43; cycle 0004 review confirmed), so AC1 is a regression check only. Remaining work: add a CI check (e.g. in check-fr11 or a script) that flags invisible characters in source files. Optionally copy unchanged text runs by slice in parseJsonc to cut memory (security low finding, cycle 0003).
acceptance_criteria: Given the plugin source, When inspected, Then the BOM constant is written as the ASCII escape "\ufeff" and the file contains no raw U+FEFF.
Given a source file containing a raw invisible character, When the CI check runs, Then it exits non-zero.

items.title: CHANGELOG missing v0.1.0 (F-001) entry
items.description: state.json records v0.1.0 released in cycle 3 for F-001, but CHANGELOG.md only lists 0.0.1. CI releaser should backfill the [0.1.0] entry (can be done alongside the next release).
acceptance_criteria: Given CHANGELOG.md, When an automated check reads it, Then it has a `## [0.1.0]` section mentioning F-001 and the version in VERSION has a matching section.

items.title: Placeholder resolver test hardening
items.description: Review info findings (cycle 0004) on backend/test/plugin/placeholders.test.ts: the inherited-env-names test would pass without the own-property check; the 1 MiB cap is only tested at cap+1. Security info finding 5 (cycle 0004): also check length after reading to cover /proc pseudo-files reporting size 0 and files grown after stat (TOCTOU).
acceptance_criteria: Given an env created via Object.create({INH:'x'}), When {env:INH} is resolved, Then it is unresolved (test fails if the own-property check is removed).
Given a file of exactly 1 MiB, When read with the default reader, Then it resolves; at 1 MiB + 1 it does not.
Given a reader result longer than the cap, When resolved, Then it is treated as unresolved.
Given shared {toString:'x'} merged into {} in defaults mode, When mergeConfig runs, Then target.toString is the own value 'x' (test fails if the own-property read guard is removed).

items.title: Optional allowlist for {file:} and {env:} placeholders
items.description: Security finding 2 (accepted risk in cycle 0004): the shared config can read any env var or user-readable file. Add an optional allowlist/path-prefix limit configurable in settings to reduce exfiltration blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Given an allowlist of env names and path prefixes, When a placeholder outside it is resolved, Then it is unresolved and reported by name only.
Given no allowlist configured, When resolving, Then behaviour is unchanged (backwards compatible).

items.title: mergeConfig hardening: visited set and sparse arrays
items.description: Security/review low+info findings in backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts: containsApiKey keeps no visited set (exponential on local graphs with shared references); sanitizeShared uses node.map which keeps sparse holes instead of null per ADR-0005 (copy with an index loop).
acceptance_criteria: Given a local config reusing the same object in many places (30 levels, 2 refs each), When mergeConfig runs in enforce mode with a conflict, Then it completes quickly (WeakSet visited tracking).
Given a sparse array in shared input, When sanitized, Then holes become null as the ADR states.

items.title: CHANGELOG missing v0.3.0 (F-003) entry
items.description: Cycle 0006 backfilled CHANGELOG [0.3.0]. Remaining: make release prepare (scripts/ci.sh or a check script) fail when VERSION has no matching CHANGELOG section, so this cannot recur (0.1.0 and 0.3.0 were both missed).
acceptance_criteria: Given VERSION is X.Y.Z and CHANGELOG.md has no [X.Y.Z] section, When bash scripts/ci.sh runs, Then it exits non-zero with a clear message.
Given matching sections exist, When ci.sh runs, Then the check passes.

items.title: resolveSettings optional hardening
items.description: Optional security info items from cycle 0006: extend hasControlChar to C1 controls and bidi overrides; cap string setting values at about 1024 characters with W2. (Lone surrogates are handled in F-005.)
acceptance_criteria: Given an org/project/repo/branch/path value with C1 controls or bidi overrides, When resolved, Then it is ignored with the fixed W2 warning.
Given a value longer than the cap, When resolved, Then it is ignored with W2.

items.title: Test default az runner and kill az process tree on Windows
items.description: Cycle 0007 security low 1 / info 3 and review info 1+2: defaultRunAz (POSIX and Windows cmd.exe path) has no automated test, and a Windows timeout kills only cmd.exe so az may keep running. Kill the process tree (taskkill /T) or pass the shared AbortSignal to execFile; add tests with a stub az / az.cmd.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stub az on PATH, When the default runner runs, Then it returns the stub's trimmed stdout and sends no shell metacharacters.
Given an az that hangs on Windows, When the timeout fires, Then the whole process tree is terminated.

items.title: Document MAX_EMPTY_CHUNKS in the plugin contract
items.description: Cycle 0007 review info 3: the 1024 consecutive empty-chunk limit in fetchRemoteConfig is not in the contract; Architect to add it (plugin-interface.md / ADR-0007).
acceptance_criteria: Given the plugin contract, When read, Then it states the consecutive empty-chunk limit and the resulting error code.

items.title: Document and test Windows case-insensitive env lookup for {env:} placeholders
items.description: Moved out of F-006 (cycle 0008 PO) to keep F-006 at 8 ACs. On Windows, process.env lookups are case-insensitive while injected test envs are case-sensitive; document the behaviour of {env:NAME} through the hook and test it.
acceptance_criteria: Given the plugin contract and user docs, When read, Then they state that {env:NAME} lookups follow process.env semantics (case-insensitive on Windows, case-sensitive elsewhere).
Given a Windows CI runner and process.env with `Path` set, When `{env:PATH}` is resolved through the default env, Then it resolves; on non-Windows the test is skipped with a clear message.

items.title: Bind cache to the settings that produced it
items.description: Cycle 0008 security low 1: the cache is one fixed file not linked to org/project/repo/path/branch, so on fetch failure a cache from another repo or org can be applied. Store a settings fingerprint (no secrets) with the cache and check it on read; reconsider using the cache when settings are missing. Also from the trust-boundary ADR-0009 accepted risk: verify whether Kilo lets a project-level config override the global plugin options and document or guard it.
acceptance_criteria: Given a cache written for repo A, When the hook runs with settings for repo B and the fetch fails, Then the cache is not applied.
Given matching settings, When the fetch fails, Then the cache is still applied.

items.title: Cache and log hardening (cleanName, temp files, TOCTOU)
items.description: Cycle 0008 security/review info: cleanName should also map U+2028, U+2029 and bidi controls to '?'; remove stale *.tmp files after a successful cache write; read the cache through one fd or check length after reading (2 MiB cap TOCTOU); document cache dir permission behaviour on Windows.
acceptance_criteria: Given a placeholder name containing U+2028 or a bidi override, When logged, Then those characters are replaced.
Given an orphan cache temp file, When a write succeeds, Then it is removed.
Given a cache file that grows past 2 MiB between stat and read, When read, Then it is rejected.

items.title: Hook test hygiene: temp dirs, env allow-list, formatting
items.description: Cycle 0008 security/review info: hook.test.ts never removes its temp home dirs (use t.after); child-process tests should pass an allow-listed env, and the KILO_AZDO_* filter must be case-insensitive on Windows; fix formatting nits (hook.test.ts:19 'OPTIONS ={', mis-indented logsAfterServer in the smoke test).
acceptance_criteria: Given the hook tests, When they finish, Then no temp home directories remain.
Given lowercase kilo_azdo_project in the parent env on Windows, When the hostile-deps child runs, Then it is not passed through.
